Indianapolis by the numbers

Why does Indianapolis property tax run through Marion County?

Indianapolis and Marion County share one government, so the county offices bill and collect the tax for the city. City and county government merged effective January 1, 1970, a move known as Unigov, and Wikipedia notes it added more than 300 square miles and roughly 250,000 residents to the city.

Indianapolis is the state capital and the county seat of Marion County. The 2020 census counted 887,642 residents, the largest city in Indiana. Local government is run by a 25-member city-county council headed by the mayor.

For an owner, the result is simple. You do not pay the city one bill and the county another. The Marion County Treasurer sends one statement, and the Marion County Auditor keeps the records for deductions and tax sales.

Which Marion County offices handle what?

Three county offices touch a typical bill, and each one answers a different question.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerBills, takes payments, runs the Stop a Tax Sale process(317) 327-4444, Suite 1001
AuditorHomestead deductions, tax sale redemption and sold parcel questions317.327.4646, Suite W-125
AssessorValues property for taxAgency page on indy.gov

Both the Treasurer and Auditor sit in the City-County Building at 200 E. Washington St., Indianapolis, IN 46204, and keep hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, according to the city's property tax page.

When is Indianapolis property tax due?

Property tax is due twice a year. The 2026 dates posted by Marion County were May 11 and November 10, and a statement with two coupons arrives in April, per the Treasurer's due dates page.

Under state law the standard dates are May 10 and November 10, and a date that lands on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day. That is why May 10, 2026 became May 11. You may pay the full year on the first date or split it.

The Treasurer extends its counter hours near the fall deadline. For 2026 it opened from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on November 6, 9 and 10 and closed on Election Day and Veterans Day.

What is the penalty for paying late in Indianapolis?

A late installment costs 5 percent of the unpaid tax if you pay within 30 days and owe nothing older on that property. Wait longer, or carry back taxes on the same parcel, and the penalty is 10 percent.

The state penalty statute, IC 6-1.1-37-10, adds a further 10 percent on unpaid tax after later installment dates, and it counts mailed payments as timely if they are postmarked by the deadline.

Marion County says the date on the U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as the payment date, even when the envelope also carries a business mailing mark.

How can you pay an Indianapolis property tax bill?

You can pay online, by phone, by mail, at a bank, by text or in a drop box. The options come from the Treasurer's payment methods page.

  • Phone: 317.327.4TAX (4829) or 1.888.881.8986, with a $1.95 charge plus a $0.95 convenience fee for e-Check, or $1.95 plus 2.5 percent for cards.
  • Mail: Marion County Treasurer, P.O. Box 6145, Indianapolis, IN 46206-6145, with the parcel number on the check.
  • Bank: First Financial Bank, Merchants Bank of Indiana, Star Financial Bank or Stock Yards Bank & Trust, which may charge fees and take payments only three weeks before the due date.
  • Drop box: first floor of the City-County Building, with payments deposited by midnight on the due date counted on time.

After an online payment it can take up to five business days for the tax bill to show the new balance. Lockbox payments must be checks, not cash.

How do homestead deductions affect an Indianapolis bill?

Homeowners who live in the house can claim two deductions, and the Auditor's Office handles the application. The standard homestead deduction is the lesser of 60 percent of assessed value or $48,000, and a supplemental deduction takes 40 percent of the remaining assessed value, per the Auditor's homestead page.

An application filed by January 15 reflects on that year's bill. Putting the property into a trust, or adding or removing an owner, means filing again.

That last point matters when you sell or inherit a house. A new owner who moves in must apply on their own, and the old owner must tell the office to remove the deductions when they stop living there.

What happens when Indianapolis taxes go unpaid?

Marion County places a tax lien on homes with unpaid property tax and sells those liens at an online auction. The 2026 sale was set for October 13 through 16, and the cutoff to stop it was October 8 at 4:30 p.m.

To stop the sale an owner pays unpaid tax, penalties and special assessments, solid waste and stormwater fees, and a $325 tax sale fee. Accepted forms are cash, certified check, cashier's check or money order.

An owner whose parcel sold has one year from the sale date to redeem, or 120 days if it was offered and did not sell. The Auditor's redemption amount tool shows the figure, and our Indiana tax sale guide explains how that number is built.

What should you know about Indianapolis houses before selling?

Indianapolis covers 367.94 square miles, with 361.64 of that land, and its nine townships are Center, Decatur, Franklin, Lawrence, Perry, Pike, Warren, Washington and Wayne. Tax sale lists in Marion County are grouped by township, so the township name on your bill matters.

The mix of housing is wide. Wikipedia lists Broad Ripple, Irvington and University Heights as historic streetcar suburbs, Castleton, Eagledale and Nora as post-war suburbs, and Fountain Square, Old Northside, Lockerbie Square and Fletcher Place among historic districts.

The city averages about 42.4 inches of precipitation a year, with May the wettest month at 5.05 inches, and around 25.9 inches of snow. About 20 days a year have thunderstorms.

Large employers include Eli Lilly with 11,000 workers, Amazon with 9,000, FedEx with 7,000, Rolls-Royce with 4,000 and Allison Transmission with 2,500, and Indianapolis International Airport hosts FedEx Express's National Hub.

How is the unpaid tax handled when you sell?

At closing, the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays the tax from the seller's proceeds. State law gives the lien for property tax priority over all other liens, so it cannot be skipped.

  • Pull the current bill by parcel number from the Treasurer's site.
  • Ask the Treasurer whether the parcel has a sale date.
  • Check the Auditor's sold parcel finder if you got a notice.

Cash Home Buyers buys Indianapolis houses as-is, with the title company settling back taxes at closing, so a seller does not need to bring cash to the table.

More questions about Indianapolis, IN Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay property tax to in Indianapolis?

The Marion County Treasurer. Indianapolis and Marion County share one government, and the Treasurer's Office bills and collects the tax at 200 E. Washington St., Suite 1001.

When are Indianapolis property taxes due?

Twice a year, with 2026 dates of May 11 and November 10. State law sets the dates at May 10 and November 10, moved forward when they fall on a weekend or holiday.

What is the late penalty in Marion County?

Five percent if paid within 30 days and no older tax is owed on the parcel, and 10 percent otherwise.

How do I apply for a homestead deduction?

File with the Marion County Auditor. A filing by January 15 shows on that year's bill, and a title change such as adding an owner or moving the house into a trust requires a new filing.

What is the tax sale administration fee?

For the 2026 Marion County sale, the Treasurer listed a $325 fee on top of unpaid tax, penalties, special assessments and solid waste and stormwater fees.

Can I pay my Indianapolis tax by phone?

Yes. Call 317.327.4TAX (4829) or 1.888.881.8986 with the parcel number. Fees apply to e-Check and card payments.

Can I sell a house in Indianapolis with back taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the tax from the proceeds at closing, after the Treasurer provides a payoff.

Fort Wayne by the numbers

Where is Fort Wayne and how is the city laid out?

Fort Wayne is the county seat of Allen County in northeastern Indiana, about 18 miles west of the Ohio line and 50 miles south of Michigan. It is Indiana's second most populous city, with 263,886 residents in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 275,203.

The city sits where the St. Joseph and St. Marys rivers meet to form the Maumee River, which runs on to Lake Erie. Locals sort the city into four unofficial quadrants, split by Calhoun Street, the St. Joseph and Maumee rivers, parts of the St. Marys River and a railroad. Historic districts include Williams-Woodland Park and Forest Park Boulevard.

FactFort WayneAllen County
Area110.79 square miles660.02 square miles
2020 census263,886385,410
2025 estimate275,203402,329
Densityabout 2,387 per square mile607 per square mile
TownshipsWayne holds the oldest city areas20

Elevation is 758 feet. The city also sits on the Saint Lawrence River Divide, which separates the Great Lakes basin from the Gulf of Mexico watershed.

How did Fort Wayne grow, and why does the boundary matter?

People have lived at the rivers' meeting point for as long as 10,000 years. The Miami settled the village of Kekionga there in the 1690s, and a trading post followed around 1706. General Anthony Wayne built Fort Wayne after the Battle of Fallen Timbers on August 20, 1794. The town was platted in 1823 and became a city on February 22, 1840.

The boundary has moved in recent memory. On January 1, 2006, the city annexed about 12.8 square miles of Aboite Township and a small part of Wayne Township, adding 25,094 people. A 2004 law also raised the population threshold for first-class city status from 250,000 to 600,000, which would otherwise have triggered consolidation with the county.

For a seller, the jurisdiction question is practical. Inside the city limits, the city's housing code and Neighborhood Code office apply. Assessment and billing run through Allen County either way.

What is the Fort Wayne economy built on?

Fort Wayne has a mixed base of manufacturing, health care, distribution and finance. The 2017 metro economy was worth $25.7 billion, and manufacturing was the largest sector at $8.1 billion.

  • Distribution, transportation and logistics employ 23.1% of Allen County workers.
  • Health care employs 17.9%, and manufacturing employs 16.9%.
  • Professional and business services employ 12.1%, and leisure and hospitality 11.1%.
  • General Motors is the largest manufacturer, with 4,320 employees in 2024.
  • Steel Dynamics is the only Fortune 500 company headquartered in the city.

Parkview Health and Lutheran Health Network are headquartered in the city, with more than 1,600 patient beds between them. Other large employers include Amazon, Lincoln Financial Group and BFGoodrich, and defense employers include BAE Systems, L3Harris and the Fort Wayne Air National Guard Base. The first phase of a Google data center was completed in December 2025. Allen County is also home to Franklin Electric, Vera Bradley and Do it Best.

What do floods and storms mean for a Fort Wayne house?

Fort Wayne has real flood history, and buyers know it. The Great Flood of 1913 killed seven people, left about 15,000 people homeless and damaged more than 5,500 buildings. It remains the worst natural disaster in city history. In 1982, about 9,000 residents were evacuated, 2,000 buildings were damaged and losses came to $56.1 million in 1982 dollars.

The climate is humid continental. Annual precipitation averages 38.34 inches and snowfall about 33.5 inches. The city averages about 39 thunderstorm days a year. The record high was 106 degrees on June 28, 2012 and the record low was minus 24 on January 12, 1918.

A seller with a basement should keep records of any waterproofing or sump pump work. A roof that has lasted through hail or wind seasons is easier to explain with dated invoices.

How does Allen County value Fort Wayne houses?

Allen County's 2025 ratio study narrative shows an assessor that watches Fort Wayne closely. It describes the Allen County market as strong, a seller's market, and says permits, listings and verifications for pre-sale remodels rose sharply.

TopicWhat the study says
Sales windowJanuary 1 to December 31, 2024, with no time adjustment
Sales checksCalls to buyers and sellers, MLS lookups and a field inspection of each validated sale
Rental housesValued with a gross rent multiplier model
Oldest city areasWayne Township, where effective age adjustments are more common
Land orderApproved after a February 20, 2025 filing, effective January 1, 2025

The county tracks work on houses in several ways. Fort Wayne's building department sends permits to the county system each night. City Utilities reports on long water shut-offs and restarts, which can signal a remodel or a demolition without a permit. The fire department reports fire-damaged properties for review. The study lists 25 reasons a sale can be marked invalid, including auction, foreclosure, short sale and family relationship, so a sale between relatives may not set a neighbor's value.

The 2024 cycle reviewed residential and agricultural parcels in Adams, Lake and Washington townships. Wayne Township, where the oldest areas of Fort Wayne sit, was in phase 3, with 25% of each property class reviewed. The target is 25% per class with a 2% tolerance. Effective age uses a county calculator, and a 1960s ranch neighborhood in the study is graded C, with homes from C-1 to C+2.

What city rules apply when I sell a Fort Wayne house?

The Neighborhood Code Compliance office in the city's Community Development Division enforces housing standards. It is at 200 E. Berry St., Suite 320, Fort Wayne, IN 46802. Call 311 or 260-427-1127.

  • Its listed programs include weed control, abandoned and inoperable vehicles, orders to demolish and orders to repair.
  • Owners of residential property who do not live in it must register it with Neighborhood Code, using the city's housing registration form.
  • Residential standards sit in Chapter 152, Housing and Building Standards.
  • A cited owner may submit a work plan to request more time, and can ask for an on-site meeting with a code officer.
  • Complaints about residential properties are filed by calling 311.

Orders to repair go through a repair hearing docket, and orders to demolish go through a hearing docket. Buyers and title companies are likely to ask about open orders, so check with the office early.

How do caps, penalties and appeals affect a Fort Wayne sale?

Indiana caps the bill at 1% of gross assessed value for a homestead, 2% for other residential property, including rentals, and 3% for nonresidential property. The homestead cap needs the homestead standard deduction, and the homestead covers the house, a garage and up to one acre.

Late payment brings a 5% penalty within 30 days if there is no earlier delinquency, and 10% otherwise, with another 10% of the unpaid principal at later installment dates. Payments are applied to tax before penalties.

An appeal starts with Form 130 and ends, if you keep going, at the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131. The board of appeals has three or five members chosen by the county commissioners and county council, and the assessor sits as a non-voting member. You may pay on the prior year's assessment while the appeal is pending. Closing through a title company clears whatever is owed from your proceeds.

What should I know about schools, roads and utilities in Fort Wayne?

Fort Wayne Community Schools is the largest public district in Indiana, with nearly 31,000 students in 2013 and 2014. East Allen County Schools, Northwest Allen County Schools and Southwest Allen County Schools serve the surrounding area. The county also has Purdue Fort Wayne with 14,192 students.

  • Interstate 69 and the I-469 beltway serve the southern and eastern edges. U.S. 24, 27, 30 and 33 cross the city, and the city has no urban freeway system.
  • Fort Wayne International Airport is the state's second busiest, and the Airport Expressway ties it to I-69.
  • Citilink buses carry about 2.2 million riders a year, though fewer than 1% of residents commute by public transit.
  • City Utilities is Indiana's largest municipally owned water utility and supplies about 72 million gallons a day from the St. Joseph River.
  • Indiana Michigan Power supplies electricity, NIPSCO supplies gas and GFL Environmental handles solid waste and recycling.

More questions about Fort Wayne, IN Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay property tax to in Fort Wayne?

You pay the Allen County Treasurer. The city does not assess or bill property tax. The Allen County Assessor sets values and hears appeals.

Does Fort Wayne require me to register a rental house?

Fort Wayne requires owners of residential property who do not live there to register it with Neighborhood Code Enforcement. Call 311 for the form and instructions.

Can I sell a Fort Wayne house with open code violations?

Yes. Open orders are likely to come up with a buyer or title company, so disclose any repair or demolition orders. A work plan lets a cited owner ask for more time, and a code officer can meet on site.

What was the 1913 flood in Fort Wayne?

It was the worst natural disaster in city history, with seven deaths, about 15,000 homeless residents and more than 5,500 damaged buildings. A 1982 flood evacuated 9,000 residents.

Why did my Fort Wayne assessment change after a remodel?

Permits go to the county each night and feed the effective age calculation. Work done before a sale also draws attention, since the study says permits for pre-sale remodels rose sharply.
